resources.string: When enabled, Izuki JS can inject gestures and read the on-screen node tree to run automation scripts.
The script running notification is always kept; this switch only controls the progress style and notify.progress updates.
Allow scripts to update the running notification through notify.progress; when disabled the API returns false.
Notification permission is not granted, so progress notifications will not appear.
How the log overlay appears while a script runs. Collapsed keeps only the title bar and stop button to avoid covering the screen.
Choosing Off closes the current overlay; you can still enable it manually on this page. Script keep-alive uses the run notification and is unaffected.

Records frame time, memory/GC, screenshots, image/color matching, OCR and log rendering metrics, reported every 30 seconds to the in-app log (prefixed with [perf]) and logcat. Read with adb logcat -s IzukiPerf.
Turn on only when comparing before/after optimizations or investigating jank; keep it off for daily use.

Read app usage records to determine the foreground app and usage time.

Allow scripts to enumerate installed apps (required on Android 11+).
Allow scripts to read / write any file on shared storage (e.g. /sdcard paths).
Allow scripts to reach the network via http.request / get / post for webhooks, verification-code services and more. Off by default; an allowlist is recommended.
Comma-separated. Leave empty to allow any host; otherwise only these hosts and their subdomains are allowed. Only http / https are supported.
Keep the CPU awake while a script runs, so screen-off / doze does not interrupt it.
Wake the screen when a script runs (may stay on the lock screen).
Wake and try to unlock the device before manual runs and scheduled tasks. Requires Shizuku or Root.
The MCP service reuses the credentials saved here; the states below are controlled from MCP service → Tool toggles.
Enable Shizuku or Root before using automatic unlock.
Digits only; encrypted with Android Keystore and never written to logs.
The screen will be locked and woken automatically. Complete the unlock on the lock screen; recording stops automatically when the device is unlocked. The full unlock action is supported.
Ongoing notification while recording a lock-screen unlock
Complete the lock-screen unlock; recording stops automatically
The device is not locked. It will be locked automatically and unlocked again.
A wrong PIN or incorrect recording may trigger system throttling or a wipe. Use only on your own device, and prefer PIN.
The screen will be locked automatically; record your normal unlock and recording stops when the device unlocks. The recording is encrypted locally.

Stop the script automatically after the selected duration to avoid runaway loops or a stuck device. Choose \"Unlimited\" to stop only manually.
Add this app to the battery optimization allowlist; otherwise the system may kill the process when you switch apps or lock the screen, interrupting scripts or the MCP server.
Battery optimization not ignored yet; may be killed in the background.

Shared by all scripts by default; same-name script variables take precedence.
One per line; blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.

These values directly affect low-level behavior; extreme values may cause jank, timeouts or service failures. Re-run scripts after changes; items marked "takes effect after restarting MCP" require restarting the MCP service.
MCP idle timeout and max client threads take effect after restarting the MCP service.
Tap %1$d more times to unlock developer options
Developer options are unlocked; open them at the bottom of Settings
Interval between frames used to detect continuous animation before uiautomator dumps the node tree; smaller is more sensitive but uses more power.
Reuse a recent probe result for the same screen; 0 probes every time.
Press duration for taps injected by the accessibility backend.
Press duration for taps injected by the Bluetooth HID backend.

Longest press duration used when a script gesture is recognized as a tap; must exceed the minimum.
Time between adjacent gesture samples when a script does not specify one.
Maximum time to wait for a new screen frame; falls back to the latest frame.
Retry count while continuous capture has no cached frame yet.
Default timeout for script http.* calls that do not specify one.
Maximum bytes read from one response; 1048576 = 1 MiB.
Maximum bytes allowed for scripts imported via subscriptions, MCP or network; 1048576 = 1 MiB.
Maximum characters of a script exception written to logs.
Sessions idle longer than this are pruned when the session table approaches capacity.
Session table capacity; the least recently used sessions are evicted first.
Maximum idle time for one client connection; takes effect after restarting the MCP service.
Thread pool limit for client connections; takes effect after restarting the MCP service.
Minimum interval between log floating-bar redraws.
Maximum log lines retained and shown in the floating bar.
Maximum results returned by one match operation.
Default for findColors and similar APIs when maxRegions is omitted.

Default interval for the wait tool when omitted.

Upper bound for UI settling; the default must not exceed it.
Preferred backend for reading the screen (screenshots, node tree); choose among ready backends only.
Preferred backend for injecting gestures / keys / text and running Shell; choose among ready backends only.

Assign a backend per capability; unassigned capabilities follow the global setting above. Only items with at least two available backends are listed.
When disabled, the backend no longer participates in capability negotiation; existing connections (such as the accessibility service or Shizuku) are unaffected.
Runs the target app on a virtual display created by Shizuku while the main screen stays usable. Requires Android 10+ and Shizuku authorization.
Lets scripts use background mode via @env RUN_MODE=background or virtualScreen.start().
Authorize Shizuku first; Android 10+ is required.
Follows the current orientation; when the long side exceeds %4$d it scales down proportionally with dpi (currently %1$d×%2$d@%3$d).

Experimental: request status/navigation bar insets on the virtual display. Some ROMs ignore it; turn it off if layout breaks.

No Shell backend is available, so touch input is disabled.
Tap, long-press or swipe the preview to operate the virtual screen.
Affects the file size of saved screenshots and the upload traffic of online OCR; image matching, color finding and local recognition still use full resolution, so coordinates are unaffected.
Low-end devices can switch to online recognition to save local compute; online failures fall back to local automatically.
Clear all log files? This cannot be undone.
